layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting resistance of a series of experimental stainless steels with varying amounts of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel, chromium, molybdenum, manganese, and nitrogen and a number of commercial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels and nickel based alloys has been studied in highly concentrated chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: media. The results show that nitrogen enhances the pitting resistance of stainless steel, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exceptional corrosion resistance is achieved with high levels of nitrogen in combination with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suitable amounts of molybdenum and chromium. For example, an alloy with 20% nickel, 24%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium, 6% molybdenum, 0.44% nitrogen, and balance iron exhibits corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noticeably better than Hastelloy alloy G and at least as good as Hastelloy alloy C-276(1) in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments investigated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effects of alloying elements on pitting resistance of stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel have been studied by many investigators. According to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kolotyrkin's early review paper,1 the beneficial elements are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr, Mo, Ni, and N. Si is also known to improve the resistance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some cases.2,3 Lorenz, et al.,4 however, reported a relatively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small influence of Ni, N, and Si additions. The role of Mn is not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: certain, since no effect was reported by Lorenz, et al., while an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increase of about 100 mV in pitting potential was reported as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Mn content increased from 1.9 to 11.2%.⁵ As far as Cr and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo are concerned, there seems to be a universal agreement on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their strong beneficial effects on pitting resistance.1,4-13

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Beneficial effects of nitrogen were reported for 18-8

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel at a level of 0.24%,14 and also when it was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: added with Mo and Si.13 Some of the studies15,16 done with Cr-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ni-Mn alloys also reported improvement due to N additions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but the exact role of N was partially clouded because of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changes in the content of Cr and Mo. Eckenrod, et al.,17

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reported that increasing N to 0.25% in 18 Cr-8 Ni steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulted in improved corrosion resistance as characterized by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lower critical and passive currents, a wider passive region, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher pitting potentials. The resistance of tempered 25 Cr 5 Ni

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Mo steel also increased sharply when it was alloyed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.5% and especially 0.7% N,18 although one would expect a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strong effect of the stabilization of austenite in this case. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the study of the pitting resistance of 18 Cr-18 Mn stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel, Hartline19 reported dual effects of N. For steels having a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplex structure, as in the previous example, the effect of N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was to increase the amount of austenite, which is superior to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferrite in Cl- environments, at a rate of about 200 times the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: percent nitrogen. The nitrogen addition to the totally austen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itic stainless steel increased the pitting resistance at the rate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of about 0.31 V per percent nitrogen added. Those observa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions lead to a conclusion that N would be a beneficial element

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a number of alloys if they are properly heat treated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the work that is described in this paper, effects of N,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, Ni, and Mn in high Cr steels were studied with the objec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive of establishing more firmly their effects on pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance. In this process, we found at least one combination

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that showed pitting resistance comparable to that of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hastelloy alloy C276 at a much lower cost. Special attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was paid to combined effects of Mo and N, as expected from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the effects of Mn substitution for part of Ni. Mn, which is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moderate austenite former, increases the nitrogen solubility.22

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other work.20,21Another objective in this study was to examine

layout_dets.text: Experimental Procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The stainless steels evaluated in this study were prepared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from commercially pure grades of Fe, Ni, ferrochrome, Mn, Mo,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Si, manganese or chromium nitride, and chromium carbide.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Melting was done in a vacuum induction furnace. The melting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: procedure consisted of: (1) melting Fe, Ni, Mo, Mn, and fer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rochrome in a vacuum; (2) bleeding nitrogen into the furnace;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and (3) introducing MnN or CrN, wrapped in iron foil, into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: melt, as needed. After casting, only solid sections of the in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gots were taken to prepare test specimens. The sections were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first soaked for 30 minutes and hot rolled. The temperatures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were 1205 C and 1095 C, depending upon hot ductility of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heats. The hot rolled specimens were pickled in a solution con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining 10% HNO₃ and 2% HF at 65 C to remove the hot work-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing scale, cold rolled to 2 mm, annealed at 1065 C for 5

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: minutes, water quenched, and pickled again in the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HNO₃-HF solution at 65 C. A small section was cut from each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heat and used for chemical analysis. Table 1 shows the com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: positions of the experimental heats.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since a relatively large number of experimental alloys was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prepared, it was necessary to conduct some rapid tests to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: screen them. These were immersion tests in ferric chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution or a combination of acid, ferric, and cupric chlorides,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and anodic polarization tests in 1 N NaCl solution at 30 C, con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ducted as follows.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specimens were cut from the processed strip into 2.5 cm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Polarization Test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Strips of 1.25 cm × 1.25 cm of the experimental alloys, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as the commercial alloys, were subjected to anodic polar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ization in dearated 1 N NaCI solution at 30 C. A Type 308 rod

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was welded to one side of each specimen and covered with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rubber tubing, except the tip for electrical connection to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiostat. The specimens were then mounted in epoxy,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground to 600 grit, and rinsed with distilled water. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specimen/mount interface was covered with a thin film of lac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quer, and approximately 1 cm² of the specimen was exposed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: They were then kept in a desiccator until testing. The testing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: procedure consisted of: (1) introduction of the solution to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one liter polarization cell; (2) setting the temperature of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution; (3) deoxygenating the solution with prepurified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen at the rate of 90 ml/min starting 30 minutes before im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mersion of the specimen; (4) cleaning the specimen with dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tilled water just prior to transferring to the cell; and (5) anodic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarization 50 minutes after the immersion at a scanning rate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 20 mV/min, using a PAR Model 173 potentiostat and ELS-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CINT Model ABA-26 Automatic Baseline Advance. The temper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ature of the solution in the polarization cell was held constant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the help of a Braun contact thermometer in conjunction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a Versa-Therm Model 2149-2 temperature controller. All

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential scans were started from the corrosion potential and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the data were autographically recorded on a Hewlett-Packard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Model 7047-A X-Y recorder. All potential data were recorded vs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a saturated calomel electrode.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The experimental alloys that exhibited good corrosion re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance in the preliminary tests and some of the commercial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys were further tested by anodic polarization in more ag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gressive environments in terms of higher chloride ion concen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tration, higher temperature, and lower pH. The experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: procedures were similar to those described in the previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paragraph, except that these tests were done with a PAR

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Model 350 Corrosion Measurement System, using a scan rate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 6 mV/min.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The corrosion resistance of the experimental alloy show-

layout_dets.text: ing the most promising results in the above tests were further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared with that of some of the highly corrosion resistant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel base alloys such as Hastelloy alloy G and especially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy C-276, by conducting a crevice corrosion test in ferric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Results and Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Preliminary Immersion and Polarization Tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results of the preliminary immersion tests in ferric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride and the anodic polarization tests in deaerated 1 N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NaCl solution at 30 C are shown in Table 2. The weight loss of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the specimens in ferric chloride varied widely and some of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimental and commercial alloys did not suffer any meas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: urable weight loss. Most of the alloys exhibited active-passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior during anodic polarization. The critical pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Table 2 is defined as the potential beyond which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the anodic current density increases very rapidly, thus in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dicating breakdown of passivity and propagation of actively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: growing pits. Therefore, a metal with a more noble Eç value in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an environment is more resistant to localized corrosion com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pared to a metal with a less noble Ec value in the same en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vironment.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accompanied by more noble Ec values. There were, however, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: few exceptions. For example, alloy 15 with no weight loss in

layout_dets.text: ferric chloride displayed a rather low EC value of 249 mV, and

layout_dets.text: The present alloy development program was initiated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: response to the need for more corrosion resistant alloys for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fer repeated corrosion failures.32,33 However, because of its

layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The corrosion resistance of austenitic Fe-Cr-Ni-Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels in chloride and acid chloride media can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significantly improved by addition of nitrogen. One high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen bearing (0.44 N) alloy offers corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparable to that of Hastelloy alloy C-276.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Since nitrogen can replace some of the nickel in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy and part of the argon used during manufacturing of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy, considerable cost saving is possible by using nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a constituent of the alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Manganese does not seem to significantly improve the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of stainless steel in the environment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under investigation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Further work is needed to manufacture larger heats of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some of the nitrogen bearing alloys and test them in order to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assess their commercial viability.
